title: Attorney General of Michigan

context.text: The seat is open: incumbent Democrat Dana Nessel is term-limited. The Michigan Bureau of Elections' candidate listing for the November 3, 2026 general election names six candidates: Eli Savit (Democratic), Doug Lloyd (Republican), Jeff Polonowski (Green), Jason Dye (Libertarian), John Perry Ludtke Jr. (U.S. Taxpayers) and Doug Dern (Natural Law).

All six were nominated at party conventions rather than a primary; the state listing records filing dates of August 31, 2026 for Savit and Dern, August 24 for Lloyd, August 3 for Polonowski, July 20 for Ludtke and June 29 for Dye.

Allegation, not a finding: in April 2026 a complaint filed with the Michigan Department of State by Bob Labrant, an attorney and former leader with the Michigan Chamber of Commerce, alleged that Savit improperly used a Washtenaw County-provided gas card for campaign travel. Savit's campaign said the county compensation package allows him personal use of a county vehicle and called the complaint meritless; the campaign also said he would voluntarily reimburse the county for gas purchases since launching his campaign. The source does not report any finding or outcome.

candidates.name: Eli Savit
candidates.ballotNote: Democratic Party nominee; filed August 31, 2026 following the party convention (Michigan Bureau of Elections listing).

priorities.text: Prosecuting and preventing serious crime, including expanded capacity for sex crimes, domestic violence and child abuse cases and community programs to prevent gun violence.
Consumer and worker protection, including enforcement against wage theft, price gouging and deceptive practices.
Environmental enforcement against polluters and protection of constitutional and civil rights.

positions.summary: His campaign says he litigated alongside Governor Whitmer to overturn Michigan's abortion ban and led national coalitions of prosecutors advocating for abortion rights at the U.S. Supreme Court.
positions.quote: When Roe v. Wade was overturned, Eli personally litigated alongside Governor Whitmer to overturn Michigan’s antiquated abortion ban.

record.text: As Washtenaw County prosecutor, filed a first-of-its-kind lawsuit declaring a fraternity's culture of sexual assault a public nuisance after more than a dozen reported assaults; his campaign says the suit forced the fraternity's closure.

Established a stand-alone workers' and consumers' rights unit, a conviction integrity and expungement unit, and special-victims and domestic violence units in the Washtenaw County prosecutor's office, according to his campaign.

candidates.researchNotes: Record items are the campaign's description of his county office; no county press releases or court filings were loaded.

statements.quote: reforms geared towards keeping firearms out of the hands of dangerous individuals
statements.context: From the issues page of his campaign website, which says he advocated for legislative changes of this kind and built community programs to prevent gun violence

candidates.name: Doug Lloyd
candidates.ballotNote: Republican Party nominee; filed August 24, 2026 following the party convention (Michigan Bureau of Elections listing).

priorities.text: Prosecuting criminals "fairly, without political favor or bias," protecting victims, and upholding the rule of law.
Standing against what his site calls political lawfare and weaponized prosecutions, and rooting out corruption and political overreach.
Advising lawmakers in crafting strong laws for Michigan.

record.text: Has led the Eaton County prosecutor's office since 2013, which his campaign says handles about 6,000 cases a year and runs domestic violence, drug and economic crimes units.

candidates.researchNotes: No positions on the fixed issue list were found on his campaign site or in coverage that could be loaded; Detroit News and Detroit Free Press coverage was blocked to automated access.
